ingredientSections.heading: Lamb
items: ½ Cup Rice Bran, Grapeseed or similar high smoke point Oil

ingredientSections.heading: Roast Vegetables
items: Rice Bran, Grapeseed or similar high smoke point Oil

ingredientSections.heading: Gravy
items: 2 Cups Stock (beef, chicken or even vegetable)

methodSections.heading: Lamb
steps: Mix the salt, paprika, dried thyme and cumin together, rub all over the leg and then cover and place in the fridge overnight.
Temper the lamb – let sit at room temperature for at least an hour (this will help the lamb cook more evenly).
Score the fat on the leg trying not to cut into the meat.
Remove the stems from the fresh thyme and rosemary, chop the leaves finely and mix into the oil.
Spread about three quarters of the fresh herb oil all over the leg and place on a roasting tray and into the preheated oven. Reserve the remaining herb oil.
Roast until internal temperature (near the bone) is 60°C (145°F) for medium rare, 70°C (160°F) for medium and 77°C (170°F) for medium-well.

methodSections.heading: Roast Vegetables
steps: Leaving the potatoes whole and the skin on, coat in oil, salt and pepper and roast until soft; roughly 45 minutes.
When soft press with the bottom of a pot or large spoon until the skin breaks and they are flattened.
Coat with the remaining herb oil and roast again until crispy on the outside. This can be done ahead of time and then reheated for service.
Trim the green tops of carrots leaving roughly an inch and then peel. If the carrots are quite small (young) you can scrub with a wire brush instead of peeling.
Coat in oil, salt and pepper, splash with sherry vinegar and roast until soft. This can be done ahead of time and then reheated for service too.

methodSections.heading: Gravy
steps: In the same pan that the lamb was roasted add the flour to drippings over a medium-low heat and stir together forming a roux.
Deglaze with the red wine and stir while it cooks off.
Add stock and simmer until liquid has thickened.
